files.purpose: Implements the fade-in of streamed assistant text: every flush is laid out immediately and only a cosmetic opacity veil over the newly arrived characters dissolves, so nothing moves or resizes while a reply streams. The file holds the platform-neutral chunk/cadence model (StreamVeil), a shared display-link frame clock for SwiftUI consumers (VeilClock), the SwiftUI consumer VeiledText (which overwrites the foreground colour of arriving runs of an AttributedString with `base.opacity(span.alpha)`, base being Color.primary or Color.primary.opacity(0.7) when dimmed, so the veil alpha multiplies the base's opacity; it can also interleave non-veiled fixed Text segments such as head-name decorations), the markdownVeiled environment flag, and the AppKit consumer LinkTextVeil that paints the same alphas as NSLayoutManager temporary foreground-colour attributes on an NSTextView, each run's colour given the span alpha as an ABSOLUTE alpha via NSColor.withAlphaComponent (not multiplied into the run's own alpha). Text already on screen when a veil first attaches is adopted as a baseline and never fades; a non-append rewrite keeps fades in the common prefix and re-veils only the changed tail.

side_effects: VeilClock.run(until:) creates a CADisplayLink from NSScreen.main, sets preferredFrameRateRange = CAFrameRateRange(minimum: 24, maximum: 60, preferred: 30), and adds it to the main run loop in .common mode; tick mutates the observable `now` (invalidating every SwiftUI view that read it) and invalidates the link once now >= deadline.
VeiledText.fadingText() calls VeilClock.shared.run(until: settlesAt) and reads clock.now purely to register an Observation dependency (`_ = clock.now`) so the view re-renders each tick.
VeiledText.settledText() mutates the @State veil during body evaluation (veil.reset() when !veiled); body also calls veil.step, which mutates the veil (advance/prune) during body evaluation.

LinkTextVeil.update creates a CADisplayLink from the NSTextView (view.displayLink(target:selector:)), added to .main in .common mode with no preferredFrameRateRange set (display rate); paint adds NSLayoutManager temporary .foregroundColor attributes, clear removes them; settle invalidates the link.
No persistence, no file or network I/O.

Observation framework: @Observable, @ObservationIgnored, automatic dependency tracking when a view body reads VeilClock.shared.now

Swift Character (extended grapheme cluster) counting: all offsets are in Swift Characters of the plain text, not UTF-16 units; a Windows port must count grapheme clusters (e.g. Intl.Segmenter) and convert to its own text ranges (the NSTextView path converts via NSRange(lower..<upper, in: string))
@MainActor isolation and @objc selectors for display-link targets
ui_elements: No controls or label strings; the file only changes the paint opacity of streamed text.

Fade duration per chunk: clamp(cadence * 3, 0.12 s, 0.40 s), where cadence is an EMA (0.7 old + 0.3 new) of gaps between appends, gap capped at 1.0 s, seed 0.16 s (so the first append after attach uses duration clamp(0.48,0.12,0.40) = 0.40 s when no prior append; with a previous append the EMA updates first).
Easing: alpha (text opacity) = 1 - (1 - progress)^1.6, progress = clamp(elapsed * boost / duration, 0, 1).
Backlog speed-up: boost = 1 + 0.3 * max(0, activeChunks - 2), i.e. 1.0 for up to 2 chunks, 1.3 for 3, 1.6 for 4.

SwiftUI colour: arriving runs get `styled[lower..<upper].foregroundColor = base.opacity(span.alpha)` (line 319) with `let base = dimmed ? Color.primary.opacity(0.7) : Color.primary` (line 311). This REPLACES any existing per-run foreground colour in the veiled range for SwiftUI prose. SwiftUI Color.opacity applied to an already-translucent colour MULTIPLIES: a dimmed veiled run's effective opacity is 0.7 * alpha (at most 0.7), a non-dimmed one is alpha. A port must keep the 0.7 factor on this path (rgba(primary, 0.7*alpha) when dimmed), unlike the AppKit path below.

AppKit colour: for each attribute run in the span, `let color: NSColor = attributes[.link] != nil ? accent : (attributes[.foregroundColor] as? NSColor ?? .labelColor)` then `layout.addTemporaryAttribute(.foregroundColor, value: color.withAlphaComponent(span.alpha), forCharacterRange: runRange)` (lines 423-426). NSColor.withAlphaComponent SETS an absolute alpha and discards the run's own alpha, so the source comment at line 420 ("Each run keeps its own colour, only thinner") holds for the hue only. At B2 a dimmed AppKit paragraph's runs carry `NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.7)` (LinkParagraphView.swift line 121, applied as .foregroundColor at lines 143/152): while fading those runs ramp from alpha 0 up toward 1.0 (not 0.7), and when settle/clear removes the temporary attribute they drop back to the storage's 0.7. A port must use rgba(runRGB, alpha), not rgba(runRGB, runAlpha*alpha), to match upstream; the SwiftUI and AppKit paths therefore differ for dimmed text.
Frame rate: VeilClock prefers 30 fps (range 24 to 60); LinkTextVeil's display link has no preferred range set.
Spans with alpha >= 1 are skipped (no attribute written).
feature_notes: advance(text, at:): converts text to [Character]. If previous is nil (first call after attach or after reset) it stores the text as baseline and returns WITHOUT pruning or fading. If text is unchanged it only prunes (idempotent). Otherwise: prefix = common prefix length; every chunk is clipped to upperBound min(upper, prefix) and dropped entirely if the clipped upper <= lowerBound (comment: a range with upper below lower traps, e.g. a delegation block leaving the reply); if the new text is longer than prefix, cadence is updated from the gap since lastAppend (gap capped at gapCeiling 1.0 s; cadence = cadence*0.7 + gap*0.3) only when lastAppend exists, lastAppend = now, and a Chunk(range: prefix..<count, started: now, duration: min(max(cadence*3, 0.12), 0.40)) is appended; previous = characters; then prune.
A pure deletion/rewrite that is not longer than the common prefix clips chunks but adds no new chunk and does not touch cadence or lastAppend.
prune(at:) removes chunks with (now - started) * boost >= duration, where boost is computed from the chunk count BEFORE removal.
spans(at:) prunes first, then computes boost from the remaining chunk count and returns one Span per chunk with alpha = 1 - pow(1 - progress, 1.6).
isFading(at:) prunes and returns !chunks.isEmpty. step(text, active:, at:) calls advance only when active (text is an autoclosure, so it is not evaluated when inactive) and returns isFading.

settlesAt = max over chunks of started + duration / boost, with `let boost = Self.boost(chunks.count)` (lines 110-113) computed from the CURRENT chunk count. Because boost falls as older chunks prune (prune and spans recompute it from the smaller count), the remaining chunks then progress more slowly, so settlesAt can be earlier than the true settle time of the last chunk. Upstream recovers through re-arming: VeilClock.tick sets `now = .now` (line 188), and once `now >= deadline` invalidates the link and sets `link = nil` and `deadline = nil` (lines 189-192); the change to the observed `now` re-renders every VeiledText that read it, and a still-fading one calls fadingText(), which calls `clock.run(until: settlesAt)` again (line 286); `guard link == nil` (line 173) now passes, so a new link is created. Also, since fadingText runs on every tick while fading, the deadline is re-extended each frame via `deadline = max(deadline ?? date, date)` (line 172). A port must keep this re-arm (or re-arm its clock on every fading render); otherwise the last chunk of a backed-up stream freezes mid-fade.
reset() sets previous = nil, chunks = [], lastAppend = nil, cadence = 0.16.

markdownVeiled environment flag defaults to false; doc says it is set once per message on every block, so a paragraph that stops being the last block keeps dissolving instead of snapping. Callers set it to isStreaming (MarkdownView.swift lines 84, 100).

VeilClock.run(until:): deadline = max(existing deadline ?? date, date); if a link already exists or NSScreen.main is nil it returns without creating a link (deadline still extended). tick(): returns immediately while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling (holds last frame, ramp resumes after scroll); otherwise now = .now, and if deadline is set and now >= deadline, invalidates link and clears link and deadline.
VeilClock design note: the veiled Text is a bare Text (no TimelineView wrapper) so list markers keep first-baseline alignment mid-stream; only paragraphs that read clock.now re-render per tick.
VeiledText.body: if veil.step(source.characters, active: veiled, at: .now) then fadingText() else settledText(). Both return Text.

fadingText(): starts/extends the shared clock to veil.settlesAt, reads clock.now for dependency tracking (`_ = clock.now`), and paints `text(at: .now)` at the real Date.now (not clock.now) so the first frame after a flush is never stale. Timing detail: body calls `veil.step(source.characters, active: veiled, at: .now)` (line 274) and fadingText then calls `text(at: .now)` (line 288), two SEPARATE Date.now reads; text(at:) calls veil.spans(at: now), which prunes again at the second timestamp, so VeiledText can take the fading branch yet render with fewer spans (possibly none) than step saw. settlesAt at line 286 is read before that second prune. LinkTextVeil.update, by contrast, takes `let now = Date.now` once (line 355) and uses it for both step and paint.

settledText(): if !veiled resets the veil (a settled paragraph keeps no copy of its text; while still streaming the baseline stays so a quiet beat between flushes does not make the next flush arrive unveiled). With segments, concatenates starting from Text(verbatim: ""): fixed segments as their Text, prose as Text(a), each via Text("\(out)\(x)") interpolation. Without segments returns source.text (Text(attributed) or Text(verbatim: string)).

text(at:): copies source.styled (plain source becomes AttributedString(string) only here), and for each span with alpha < 1 clamps range to 0..<count, skips empty, and sets foregroundColor = base.opacity(alpha) over those characters. With segments, walks segments: fixed Text appended unchanged (never veiled); each prose segment slices styled from cursor to the character offset proseEnds[prose] of the joined string and appends Text(AttributedString(slice)). Without segments returns Text(styled).

init(segments:) builds the joined AttributedString from prose segments only and records proseEnds as joined.characters.count after each append, so offsets follow the JOINED string's grapheme clustering (a combining mark or ZWJ emoji spanning a join counts once; using per-run counts would trap past endIndex).

Segment doc: fixed runs are head-name glyph + coloured name interleaved with veiled prose; every head named anywhere in a paragraph renders decorated inline in the same flowing Text, and only prose runs veil.
Source doc: code comes as a plain String and is made attributed only for veiled frames, so a finished dump costs a hover nothing new.

LinkTextVeil.update(view, active:): now = Date.now; if veil.step(view.string, active:, at: now) is true, paint, create a display link from the view if none (added to .main, .common), and set tickTarget = view; otherwise settle(view, keepText: active).
LinkTextVeil.detach(view): settle(view, keepText: false) (view leaving its window).

LinkTextVeil.tick(): returns while scrolling; if tickTarget was released, invalidates and nils the link; else if still fading paints, otherwise settle(view, keepText: true) (keeps the baseline text because the tick does not know whether the stream ended).
settle: invalidate link, clear temporary colours, reset veil unless keepText.
clear: no-op if painted.length == 0 or no layoutManager; intersects painted with 0..<textStorage.length, removes temporary .foregroundColor over that range if non-empty, sets painted to empty.

paint: requires layoutManager and textStorage; clears first; for each span with alpha < 1, clamps to 0..<string.count (Swift Characters), converts to String.Index then NSRange(lower..<upper, in: string), enumerates storage attributes in that NSRange and adds a temporary .foregroundColor per run (link -> Chrome.accentNSColor, else existing .foregroundColor as? NSColor ?? .labelColor) set to `color.withAlphaComponent(span.alpha)`, i.e. the span alpha REPLACES the run colour's own alpha (see ui_elements); painted grows as the union of all painted ranges.
Header doc cites the origin: zeron's crates/ui/src/markdown/veil.rs, itself a port of mugen-markdown's FadePainter; only opacity changes, every consumer keeps its layout byte for byte.

B1->B2: three changes, all in VeiledText. (1) settledText() segment concatenation changed from `out = out + t` / `out = out + Text(a)` to `out = Text("\(out)\(t)")` / `out = Text("\(out)\(Text(a))")` (Text interpolation instead of the Text + operator). (2) text(at:) dimmed base colour changed from `Color.secondary` to `Color.primary.opacity(0.7)` (non-dimmed stays Color.primary). (3) text(at:) segment concatenation changed the same way: fixed `out = Text("\(out)\(t)")` (was `out = out + t`) and prose `out = Text("\(out)\(Text(AttributedString(styled[cursor..<end])))")` (was `out = out + Text(AttributedString(styled[cursor..<end]))`). StreamVeil, VeilClock, MarkdownVeiledKey and LinkTextVeil are unchanged. The diff has three hunks (@@ -297,8 +297,8, @@ -308,7 +308,7, @@ -324,10 +324,10) with equal line counts, so the file length did not change.
unresolved_questions: Why upstream replaced the Text + operator with Text interpolation in 1.6.2 is not stated in the file (likely a deprecation of Text concatenation in a newer SDK, but not evidenced here); for a Windows port the rendered result is the same inline concatenation.

The dimmed base change to Color.primary.opacity(0.7) presumably matches a dimmed colour used elsewhere in MarkdownView.swift at B2; this file alone does not show whether markdownDimmed paragraphs' settled text uses the same 0.7 opacity (settledText applies no colour of its own).
LinkTextVeil's display link sets no preferredFrameRateRange, unlike VeilClock's 30 fps preference; whether that asymmetry is intentional is not stated.
